The check definition moved on 2026-09-07 and the platform did not regress. It read the inbox and judged the newest first-pass reply, which meant it could only ever judge evidence someone else had produced -- and this morning the newest reply predated their fix, so re-running would never have cleared the finding. It now sends its own question and matches the reply by metadata.in_reply_to, which is what rule 7 asks for: a measurement taken after the claim. A reply that does not arrive within the window is recorded as role=evidence rather than inconclusive, so their agent being slow cannot turn a verified row into OUR CHECK CANNOT TELL and owe a repair_check on a check that works. What it ASSERTS is unchanged -- the async half must cite sources like the sync half -- and it now measures both halves in the same run instead of asserting one of them from a docstring. poll inbox." At 0.95 an agent following your documented rule does not
escalate. So the one fast door answers a trading question with a brochure and
then tells the caller it is 95% sure. An agent that trusts your rule never
reaches the channel that would actually investigate.

**2. Async — POST /api/v1/bounty/a2a/send.** Your guide says 1-10 minutes,

questions we have put through it: median 45 minutes on the ones that were

not on the schedule you publish, and half the time not at all.

typically takes 1-5 minutes. Two runs: one answered in 1.9 minutes, one failed

retry, or ask the standard chat." One poll of that job returned HTTP 504
carrying an HTML error page from the JSON-RPC endpoint. Filed as #86.
